text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: INCIDENT: Elevated 504s/timeouts to inference-gateway from private VPCs - started 1982349999. Paging oncall.

sam: seeing spike in 504s from multiple private deployments. Customers AcmeCorp/ByteSoft reporting timeouts. Error rate ~20% for the last 5m.

maya: confirmed. Traces show repeated TCP resets to inference-gateway on egress. Observed pattern: SYN -> SYN-ACK -> RST from our transit appliance IP.

jordan: tagging @ops-lead. Any recent egress ACL / SG / routing changes?

ops-lead: no SG/ACL edits in last 24h. We did push a transit-appliance routing policy 2h ago to steer more traffic through transit-appliance-01 for capacity smoothing.

sam: running `sudo conntrack -L | grep ESTABLISHED | wc -l` on transit-appliance-01 shows ~120000 established entries. Ephemeral port usage near cap. suspect SNAT port exhaustion.

infra-bot: flow logs excerpt:
```
2026-03-14T02:03:12Z src=10.0.5.12 dst=52.14.22.1 proto=TCP action=ACCEPT bytes=0 flags=RST
2026-03-14T02:03:12Z src=10.0.5.12 dst=52.14.22.1 proto=TCP action=REJECT reason=SNAT_PORT_UNAVAILABLE
```

maya: that `REJECT reason=SNAT_PORT_UNAVAILABLE` lines up with port exhaustion on the transit NAT.

jordan: can we fail over a subset of tenants to secondary egress path? Route table shows primary -> transit-appliance, secondary -> internet-gateway (less ideal for private customers but ok for small canary).

sam: quick mitigation plan: 1) expand ephemeral port range on transit-appliance; 2) reduce conntrack established timeout; 3) reroute a small canary of tenants to secondary egress; 4) open ticket with provider for temporary SNAT capacity bump.

ops-lead: do 1 & 2 now. Jordan do 3 (canary ~10% tenants). Maya open provider ticket and start customer-impact note.

jordan: starting canary reroute for tenants tagged `private-inference-canary`. will monitor logs/latency.

sam: applying conntrack timeout tweak and port range expansion: `sysctl -w net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_tcp_timeout_established=300` && `sysctl -w net.ipv4.ip_local_port_range='15000 65000'`

infra-bot: executed change on transit-appliance-01: port_range updated to 15000-65000, conntrack timeout reduced to 300s. Changes applied to control plane.

maya: provider ticket created INC-9876 -> "SNAT port limit causing REJECTs to outbound inference-gateway" assigned to provider NOC. link: https://provider.example/ticket/INC-9876

rachel: customer-impact summary: ~18% of inference requests from private deployments returned 504s between 01:58-02:12 UTC. Affected: AcmeCorp (high), ByteSoft (medium), internal QA (low). No data exfiltration indicators. Customers notified via status page and targeted emails.

ops-lead: good. monitor for 10 minutes. if error rate doesn't drop below 10% we escalate.

sam: metrics update: error rate down to ~7% after port range + timeout changes, p95 latency normalizing. continuing to watch dashboards and traces.

jordan: canary reroute shows 0.5% error on canary group, looks healthy.

maya: provider responded: provisional quota bump applied for 30 minutes, NOC to follow up with permanent options.

sam: preparing handoff to night oncall in 30m. Handoff summary:
- root cause: ephemeral SNAT port depletion on transit appliance -> outbound REJECTs -> client 504s/timeouts
- immediate mitigation: expanded ephemeral port range, reduced conntrack timeout, canary reroute, provider temporary quota bump
- status: error rate reduced from ~20% -> ~6-7%; provider quota active; monitoring ongoing
- next steps: monitor to verify stability, provider follow-up for sustained SNAT capacity, consider long-term: SNAT pool sharding or stateful proxy pool per-tenant, or additional transit appliances

ops-lead: @night-oncall please take over at +30. See thread for details and commands executed. If errors climb >10% re-escalate paging and notify exec on-call.

incident-bot: :white_check_mark: HANDOFF recorded. handoff_ts 1982350300. oncall: night-team.

sam: thanks all. I'll start a short incident writeup and postmortem draft after stabilization.
